translationRepairs: Empress Wang of Heir Apparent Taizong bore Lamented Crown Prince Daqi and Prince of Nan commandery Dalian; Lady Chen the Shure bore Prince of Xunyang Daxin; the left lady bore Princes Dalin of Nanhai and Dachun of Anlu; Lady Xie bore Duke of Liuyang Daya; Lady Zhang bore Prince of Xinxing Dazhuang; Bao Zhaohua bore Prince of Xiyang Dajun; Lady Fan bore Prince of Wuning Dawei; Chu Xiuhua bore Prince of Jianping Daqiu; Lady Chen bore Prince of Yi'an Daxin; Lady Zhu bore Prince of Suijian Dazhi.

Empress Wang of Heir Apparent Taizong bore Lamented Crown Prince Daqi and Prince of Nan commandery Dalian; Lady Chen the Shurong bore Prince of Xunyang Daxin; the Left Lady bore Prince Dalin of Nanhai and Prince Dachun of Anlu; Lady Xie bore Duke of Liuyang Daya; Lady Zhang bore Prince of Xinxing Dazhuang; Bao Zhaohua bore Prince of Xiyang Dajun; Lady Fan bore Prince of Wuning Dawei; Chu Xiuhua bore Prince of Jianping Daqiu; Lady Chen bore Prince of Yi'an Daxin; Lady Zhu bore Prince of Suijian Dazhi.
s0003 has 陳淑容 (Shurong), not 'Shure,' and lists distinct sons 尋陽王大心 and 義安王大昕. Keeping each shared romanization attached to the prince's territorial title distinguishes them naturally in English.
In the third year the city fell; Senior Armor Xiao Shao fled south and proclaimed a secret edict making Daxin regular palace attendant and General Who Pacifies the South.
In the third year the city fell; Marquis of Shangjia Xiao Shao fled south and proclaimed a secret edict making Daxin regular palace attendant and General Who Pacifies the South.
s0015 names 上甲侯蕭韶; 上甲侯 is the marquisate title Marquis of Shangjia, so “Senior Armor” is a false calque and the proposed replacement matches the Chinese.
In the third year the city fell; Senior Armor Xiao Shao fled south and proclaimed a secret edict adding Daxin as regular palace attendant and promoting his title to General Who Pacifies the South.

In the third year the city fell; Marquis of Shangjia Xiao Shao fled south and proclaimed a secret edict adding Daxin as regular palace attendant and promoting his title to General Who Pacifies the South.
The same 上甲侯蕭韶 appears in the literal field of s0015; replacing “Senior Armor” with “Marquis of Shangjia” corrects the title without changing the rest of the sentence.
In the third year Kuaiji bandits led by Tian Ling gathered tens of thousands and attacked; Dalian ordered middle army aide Zhang Biao to strike and behead them.
In the third year Kuaiji bandits led by Tian Lingqun gathered tens of thousands and attacked; Dalian ordered middle army aide Zhang Biao to strike and behead them.
s0066 names the bandit leader 田領群; truncating to “Tian Ling” drops 群 from the given name, and “Tian Lingqun” restores the full personal name.

s0125 is the interlinear note 〈（本書不載所生，別有傳）〉; the idiomatic English left an orphan “)〉”, and wrapping the gloss in matching parentheses removes the corrupted CJK bracket without changing the note’s meaning.
In the second year, he went out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and administrator of Langye and Pengcheng commanderies, but before reaching his post he was killed, aged eleven.
In the second year, he went out as General of Peaceful Distance and administrator of Langye and Pengcheng commanderies, but before reaching his post he was killed, aged eleven.

s0189 assigns 寧遠將軍; the same title is already rendered “General of Peaceful Distance” in s0123, whereas “General Who Pacifies the Distant” misreads 寧 as “pacify,” so aligning the idiomatic gloss corrects the sense.
